items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: I remember my singing playing blues with Tate Chambers.

ctx.x: No. Mud Carey would play him and Mud Carey and Joe Johnson, the trumpet player, you know. Joe Johnson, Ernest Kelly on trombone. But they could read. See, little Joe Johnson could read. Ernest Kelly too. Ernest Kelly, Joe Johnson, Mud Carey, Tate Chambers, sometimes Bunk Johnson, the trumpet.
You remember Bunk back then, right?

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: Had old man Tatt baritone. ... When I was playing with him [Arnold] ... And Piku played with us.

ctx.x: Oh. Who were the three tracks with the Arnold one? I couldn't get that.

That's the Arnold man. When I was playing with him. Mm-hmm. When I was playing with him, there were Maurice, Manuel Perez, and that sometime Rick. Mm-hmm. And sometime another trumpet player. Uh-huh. But Maurice and Manuel was the main trumpet players. Mm-hmm. And, uh, Eddie Yank on trombone. Yank Johnson on trombone. And Piku played with us. Uh-huh. And sometime Eddie Sherry playing that.
